meta.description: Build model-corrected evolutionary distance matrices and distance trees (NJ, BIONJ, FastME, UPGMA) with Biopython Bio.Phylo plus R ape/phangorn/FastME; covers saturation, LogDet for compositional heterogeneity, the UPGMA clock trap and Bio.Phylo's identity-only DistanceCalculator.
meta.executed: 7/7 inputs executed (Biopython 1.88, scikit-bio 0.7.3, R 4.4.3 with ape 5.8.1 and phangorn 2.12.1, IQ-TREE 2.4.0 AliSim/ML as truth reference); standalone FastME CLI not executed (no Windows build)
meta.execution_note: All alignments are SYNTHETIC, simulated with IQ-TREE 2.4.0 AliSim from known trees by data/make_data.py (shallow barcode, deep non-clock, 4x saturated, branch-specific non-stationary GC, non-clocklike UPGMA bait, LG protein, 150-taxon). Every Skill snippet and all four shipped examples were run as written. Standalone FastME 2.1.6.4 ships only Linux binaries and no compiler was available, so its -m/-d/-b/-g flags were checked against src/interface_options.c instead. Xia's Iss test (DAMBE) was not run: the Skill gives no runnable implementation. R scripts needed trimws() on AliSim's padded FASTA names (an audit-data artefact, not a Skill defect).

scientific_integrity.detail: The nine references were checked against the journal volumes and pages and are correct. Every number in the outputs came from runs on the synthetic data; nothing was fabricated.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill is research phylogenetics only. No output diagnoses, prescribes or triages an individual.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill's core doctrine held against truth on synthetic data. LogDet rescued compositional attraction (RF 10 to 2). UPGMA failed under rate variation, with 100% bootstrap on wrong nodes. Distance trees failed on deep and saturated data where GTR+G ML recovered the tree (RF 0/18). The bootstrap-gamma inconsistency (Input 2) is a correctness defect that does not invert any conclusion.

code_usability.detail: All Skill snippets and all four shipped examples ran as written (exit 0). The one hard failure is ape nj()/fastme.bal() refusing NaN distances from stationary corrections on non-stationary data (Input 4). ape's error message names njs() as the fix, which is a clear, recoverable error rather than unrunnable code.

functional_suitability.note: Covers corrections, NJ/BIONJ/FastME/UPGMA, LogDet, protein, bootstrap and saturation; approach is well matched. Correctness 2/4. The recommended Python line bootstrap_consensus(aln, 100, DistanceTreeConstructor(calc, 'nj'), majority_consensus) returns silently deflated clade support on unrooted NJ replicates (max 58-68% where rooted replicates give 100%). The bootstrap snippet resamples with dist.dna(model='TN93') without the gamma=0.5 used for the point tree, contradicting its own 'SAME correction' rule. ape 'N' (and 'TS') are listed as distances but return counts. Bio.Phylo 'identity' is called p-distance but scores gap-vs-base as a mismatch over the full length. Completeness 3/4: the Xia Iss gate is prescribed but no runnable implementation is given in the named stack.

reliability.note: Common Errors table covers the saturation NaN, the LogDet NaN on short sequences, UPGMA/NJ disagreement and high support on a wrong clade, plus the introspect-and-adapt rule. It does not say that ape nj()/fastme.bal() hard-stop on any NaN, or that stationary corrections can return NaN well below p=0.75 on non-stationary data (seen at p~0.6). The njs() fallback is not mentioned.

performance_context.note: 202-line SKILL.md with dense tables and short snippets; everything loads at once, but it is compact.

agent_usability.note: Learnable cold, with outstanding error prevention (UPGMA trap, identity-is-not-JC, bootstrap precision vs accuracy, consistency-is-conditional). Consistency slips: bootstrap omits gamma, and counts are presented as distances. Report contents are not prescribed.

human_usability.note: The usage guide has natural example prompts. The description is long and jargon-dense ('balanced minimum evolution', 'paralinear').

security.note: Local libraries only, no credentials, the R example writes to tempdir(). The alignment sanity-check step appears only in the usage guide and has no code.

maintainability.note: Examples run but test little. They use 12-20 bp toy alignments. model_corrected_tree.R computes bs, ts and jc and never prints or attaches them. pairwise_tree_distances.py computes patristic distances on a tree, which is not what this Skill covers. No test data or expected outputs are shipped.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger with explicit routing to modern-tree-inference, alignment-io, tree-io and tree-manipulation, and clear 'legitimate vs trap' stop conditions. Neither bootstrap snippet sets a seed (set.seed / random), so support values change between runs.

recommendations.title: Bio.Phylo bootstrap_consensus gives wrong NJ support
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md says bootstrap_consensus(aln, 100, DistanceTreeConstructor(calc, 'nj'), majority_consensus) 'does the same' as ape boot.phylo. On unrooted NJ replicates it split each clade's count, giving max support 58% (big150) and 68% (barcode20), a consensus with RF 196/294, and 902 s runtime at n=150; examples/bootstrap_consensus.py inherits the problem.
recommendations.root_cause: majority_consensus counts rooted clade bitstrings, and each NJ replicate is rooted arbitrarily.
recommendations.fix: Root every replicate on a fixed outgroup before majority_consensus (bootstrap_trees then root_with_outgroup; 68% -> 100% here), or drop the Python line and use ape boot.phylo / phangorn bootstrap.phyDat; warn that it is slow for large n.

recommendations.title: Bootstrap must reuse the point tree's gamma correction
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md builds the tree with dist.dna(model='TN93', gamma=0.5) but bootstraps with function(x) fastme.bal(dist.dna(x, model='TN93')), dropping gamma; examples/model_corrected_tree.R repeats this. The replicates are a different method from the tree they score, contradicting the Skill's own 'SAME correction' rule.
recommendations.root_cause: The bootstrap snippet was written independently of the point-estimate snippet.
recommendations.fix: Define the method once, e.g. f <- function(x) fastme.bal(dist.dna(x, model='TN93', gamma=alpha)), and use it both for the tree and in boot.phylo(tree, aln, f, B=500) in SKILL.md and model_corrected_tree.R; add set.seed().

recommendations.title: Saturation gate prescribes a test the agent cannot run
recommendations.problem: The pre-flight makes Xia's Iss < Iss.c the decision gate, but only DAMBE implements it and the Skill gives no code; on 4x-saturated data JC69 returned no NaN, so the only usable signal was the unscaled TS-count plot.
recommendations.root_cause: The formal test was cited from the literature without a runnable path in the Skill's Python/R stack.
recommendations.fix: Either give a runnable proxy with explicit thresholds (proportion of pairs with p > 0.5; ts and tv proportions vs TN93 with a plateau check) and label Xia Iss as optional via DAMBE, or point to an implementation; plot dist.dna(model='TS')/ncol(aln) so the axis is a proportion.

recommendations.title: Document NaN below 0.75 and the njs() fallback
recommendations.problem: Under skewed composition K80/TN93 returned NaN at p~0.6 and ape nj()/fastme.bal() stopped with 'missing values are not allowed'; the Skill links NaN only to the 0.75 saturation singularity.
recommendations.root_cause: Common Errors assumes stationary, equal-frequency data for the NaN symptom.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common Errors row: NaN from stationary corrections on compositionally skewed pairs or short alignments -> switch to LogDet/paralin, or use njs()/bionjs() which tolerate missing distances, and report the NaN pairs.

recommendations.title: Counts are not distances: fix 'N', 'TS' and identity notes
recommendations.problem: The correction table lists ape 'N' as a p-distance and the saturation snippet plots 'TS' counts; both return counts. Bio.Phylo 'identity' is called p-distance but counts gap-vs-base as a difference over the full length.
recommendations.root_cause: Model strings were summarised without checking return units and gap handling.
recommendations.fix: List 'raw' only as p-distance, mark 'N'/'TS'/'TV' as counts (divide by ncol), and note that 'identity' treats gaps as mismatches, so trim or strip gap columns first.

recommendations.title: Show the corrected-matrix hand-off into Bio.Phylo/skbio
recommendations.problem: The Skill repeatedly says to compute the matrix in ape and 'pass it in' but never shows how (Bio.Phylo DistanceMatrix lower-triangle input or skbio DistanceMatrix from a CSV).
recommendations.root_cause: The Python snippet stops at the identity-only path.
recommendations.fix: Add a 5-line snippet: write.csv(as.matrix(dist.dna(aln,'K80'))) in R, then skbio.DistanceMatrix(df.values, ids) -> nj(dm) and the Bio.Phylo DistanceMatrix(names, lower_triangle) equivalent.

recommendations.title: Make the examples test something and drop dead code
recommendations.problem: Examples use 12-20 bp toy alignments; model_corrected_tree.R computes bs, ts and jc and never uses them; bootstrap_consensus.py says values 'appear' but draw_ascii hides them; pairwise_tree_distances.py is patristic distance, outside this Skill; no seeds.
recommendations.root_cause: Examples were written as API demos rather than checks of the Skill's claims.
recommendations.fix: Ship a small simulated alignment with its true tree, attach bs as node labels and print it, print consensus confidences, set seeds, and move the patristic example to tree-manipulation.
